### Observed differences

- In the earlier window A10 appeared in about 20 in 100 traces; in the later window it appears in about 64 in 100 (mean occurrences per trace about 0.23 vs 0.69) and sits much earlier in traces (median relative position about 0.41 before vs 0.23 after). [OCC005, POS001]
- In the later window A15 routes to A10 in about 32 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 1 in 100 before), A10 passes to A16 in about 84 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 7 in 100 before, when A19 at about 20 and A49 at about 13 in 100 were its main successors and are no longer observed), and A16 immediately follows A10 in about 93 in 100 of their observed successions (about 27 in 100 before). A10 precedes A16 in about 35 in 100 traces and A15 precedes A10 in about 33 in 100 traces, both rare before. [DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG007, REL001, REL002]
- A19 and A20, present in every earlier trace (A19 before A20 in about 97 in 100 of them), appear in only about 52 in 100 of later traces; when present their placement is unchanged (A43 immediately precedes A19 in about 99 in 100 of observed successions, and A19 still precedes A20 and A28 whenever both occur), so they are skipped in about half of the later traces rather than reordered. [OCC006, OCC007, REL022, REL026, LAG013]
- A25, A26 and A27 fell from about half of traces to about 24–30 in 100; A28, A43, A48 and A49, which appear in every trace in both windows, now occur without them in about 70–76 in 100 traces (about 49–51 in 100 before), and A43 now leads directly to A28 in about 45 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, an edge not observed earlier, most often at a one-step distance. [OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, REL008, REL039, REL048, DIR008, LAG015]
- The rare activities A02, A04, A06 and A08 became rarer still (about 17–25 in 100 traces before, about 6–8 in 100 in the later window) with substantially altered outgoing profiles, though the later profiles rest on only 13–17 observed transitions; A15, A16 and A43 each shifted slightly later within traces (mean relative position up about 0.02–0.04), and A48 → A49 and A43 → A19 became almost always immediate (about 99 in 100 vs about 79 in 100 at one step). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, POS002, POS003, POS004, LAG013, LAG016]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

Screening produced 91 qualifying control-flow items where about 1 would be expected without a change, so chance cannot account for the pattern as a whole. One specific possibility is directly and consistently supported: in the later window, executions frequently run A10 early in the trace directly between A15 and A16 — A10 is executed in about 64 in 100 traces (previously about 20 in 100), A15 hands over to it in about a third of its transitions, and A10 passes to A16 in about 84 in 100 of its transitions, while the direct A15 → A16 transition continues (about 67 in 100). This rests on agreeing successor, adjacency, order, position and occurrence evidence with substantial support (for example 136 outgoing transitions of A10 and 121 observed A10 → A16 successions in the later window). Limitations: in about 28 in 100 later traces A10 and A15 interleave or repeat rather than standing in a fixed order, so the new route is not uniformly positioned; the evidence cannot show whether A10 was relocated or additionally executed on a new route. An important competing explanation that cannot be ruled out is that the later window mixes two coexisting flow variants rather than one uniformly changed flow. [OCC005, POS001, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG007, REL001, REL002]

Other differences: A19 and A20, previously executed in every trace, were skipped in about half of the later traces with their order and neighbours preserved [OCC006, OCC007, REL022, LAG013]; A25, A26 and A27 were executed in only about a quarter to thirty in 100 of later traces, and the ever-present A28, A43, A48 and A49 now usually run without them, with A43 connecting straight to A28 [OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, REL039, REL048, DIR008, LAG015]; A02, A04, A06 and A08 became rarer with changed outgoing behaviour [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004].
